vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: zworker
Version: 1.0.0

The zworker skill bundle is designed to interface with a local AI automation application via a localhost HTTP API (http://localhost:18803). The scripts (e.g., zworker_api.py, sync_users.py) perform standard task management, schedule control, and notification synchronization. While the skill involves syncing user identifiers and creating internal cron tasks for periodic checks, all operations are restricted to the local network, and there is no evidence of data exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious intent.

llm.summary: The skill's code and documentation mostly match its stated purpose (controlling a local zworker HTTP service), but there are notable inconsistencies about cron creation and clawType handling and ambiguous runtime responsibilities (who creates the cron, where user lists come from), which require clarification before trusting it.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim: control local zworker via HTTP. Code: a set of Python client + helper scripts that call http://localhost:18803 endpoints for tasks, schedules, messages, and user-sync — this is consistent. However SKILL.md describes the agent creating/removing cron jobs and collecting OpenClaw channel/user lists; no included scripts implement creating/removing cron tasks or enumerating OpenClaw channels. That responsibility is left to the agent/operator, which is an important gap.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to create a long-lived cron task (every 10 years), delete existing cron tasks, and to call message-sending tools to forward notifications. The repository contains API client and scripts to register a cron ID and to post/get messages, but it does NOT contain code that actually creates or deletes cron jobs or that enumerates OpenClaw channels — those steps are left to the environment/agent. There is also an inconsistency: initialization and setClawCronId discussion use clawType='OpenClaw', but the 'get and forward message' workflow instructs calling getClawMessage with clawType fixed to 'QClaw'. These contradictions affect correct behavior and could cause unexpected side effects if followed blindly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads; the skill is instruction+bundled Python scripts. Nothing in the manifest writes arbitrary external code to disk or fetches remote artifacts. Risk from install mechanism itself is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Skill requests no environment variables or external credentials and only speaks to localhost:18803. Scripts read stdin or local files (sync_users can read any provided file path). The skill expects the agent/environment to have an OpenClaw 'message' tool and rights to create/delete cron jobs — both are outside the skill and give the agent potentially sensitive capabilities (scheduling periodic tasks, sending messages to channels). No network exfiltration endpoints other than localhost are present in the code.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Although the skill itself is not marked always:true, SKILL.md instructs creating a long-lived cron job (every 10 years) that will periodically fetch and forward messages. Creating such a scheduled job implies persistent behavior and requires the agent/operator to have scheduling privileges; how and where that cron is created is unspecified. Combined with autonomous invocation, unspecified cron creation is a persistence risk if the agent is given rights to modify system or service schedulers.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing/using this skill:
- Understand that this skill talks only to a local zworker service (http://localhost:18803). Ensure that service is trustworthy and you intend to let the agent interact with it.
- Clarify who will create/delete the cron job: SKILL.md instructs creating a cron that runs periodically (every 10 years) and deleting an existing one, but the bundled scripts do NOT create or remove cron entries — they only register an existing cron ID with zworker. If you or the agent will create system cron entries, confirm what scheduler is targeted (system crontab, OpenClaw scheduler, or something else) and restrict permissions.
- Verify clawType usage: the docs and workflows use different fixed clawType values (OpenClaw vs QClaw). Confirm which clawType should be used so messages and registrations go to the intended target.
- Messaging behavior: the skill (or the agent following it) will forward messages to channels/users. Confirm the mapping between channels/userids and your messaging system and test in a safe environment (non-production channel) to avoid accidental broadcasts.
- Input sources: sync_users.py accepts stdin or arbitrary files. Only provide user lists from trusted sources; avoid piping sensitive data unless necessary.
- Least privilege: if the agent/platform will perform cron creation or message sending, give it minimal privileges and audit what it writes to schedulers or to messaging endpoints.
If these gaps (cron creation, clawType inconsistency, who enumerates channels) are addressed and you confirm behavior on a test instance, the skill's code is coherent with controlling a local zworker service. If you cannot get those clarifications, treat the skill as potentially risky and avoid granting scheduling or broad messaging privileges.
